statement: Three general real input circles admit at most eight distinct ordinary real circles tangent to all three.

answer.text: Three general real input circles admit at most eight distinct ordinary real circles tangent to all three.

source.location: Sections 6–7, original pp.98–99; quadratic reduction Section 4, p.97
source.version: Original Latin journal scan (1790), pp.95–101 and plate; all eight PDF pages visually inspected. Archive identifier E648; the 1779 presentation date is not a publication year.

scope: Three ordinary real circles in the noncollinear-centre regular chart; finite ordinary real solution circles, with internal and external contacts represented by signed input radii.
notes:
This records Euler’s upper bound, not a checked construction attaining eight. Special inputs outside the regular quadratic chart and infinite fibres are excluded; no claim about a singular-fibre spectrum is inherited.

Source discussion. There are at most eight distinct real solution circles. Eight contact-sign patterns initially give two quadratic roots apiece; simultaneous reversal of all three signs identifies paired roots, leaving four quadratic equations and at most eight solutions.
